classification.difficultyReason: Derive side lengths from coordinates and combine exact cosine, sine and area calculations.

content.prompt: Points $A(1,2)$, $B(4,6)$ and $C(-1,4)$ form vertices of a triangle. Find the area of $\triangle ABC$.

inlines.text: Find the side lengths from the coordinates, then use the cosine rule and the area rule.

answer.worked:
The distance formula gives
$$\begin{align*}
AB&=\sqrt{3^2+4^2},& AC&=\sqrt{(-2)^2+2^2},& BC&=\sqrt{(-5)^2+(-2)^2}\\
AB&=5,& AC&=2\sqrt2,& BC&=\sqrt{29}.
\end{align*}$$
Let $\theta=\angle BAC$. By the cosine rule,
$$\begin{align*}
\cos\theta&=\frac{5^2+(2\sqrt2)^2-(\sqrt{29})^2}{2(5)(2\sqrt2)}\\
\cos\theta&=\frac1{5\sqrt2}.
\end{align*}$$
Since $\theta$ is acute, use a right reference triangle with adjacent side $1$ and hypotenuse $5\sqrt2$. Its opposite side is $\sqrt{(5\sqrt2)^2-1^2}$, so
$$\begin{align*}
\sin\theta&=\frac{\sqrt{(5\sqrt2)^2-1^2}}{5\sqrt2}\\
\sin\theta&=\frac7{5\sqrt2}.
\end{align*}$$
Hence,
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Area}&=\frac12(5)(2\sqrt2)\left(\frac7{5\sqrt2}\right)\\
\text{Area}&=7\text{ square units}.
\end{align*}$$
